## Contract review

Local-runs: none

PR objectui#12014, round 12 of card objectui#6152 (draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #6152 (round 12)`, no closing keyword). Inputs, and nothing else: the card body and all 80 comments (the round-12 claim 6070030626, the census report 6070437445, the seat's answers 6070475966 Q1 → A / Q2 → B / Q3 → A with the amended file surface, the implementation report 6071238136, and the standing rulings the earlier rounds carry: objectui#8327, objectui#10380 ruling A, the 「改成追加说明 (Recommended)」 shape for pending changesets, and the Clause-② reading the round-7 to round-11 records PASSed), the PR body, its 26-file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge base `7ebff3991733bbe9557a2dc185b1362412b02367` (26 files, +1041 / −210, the same 26 paths as the file list), and the 43 check-runs on this head: 40 success, 3 skipped by design (dependabot, Test (coverage), Test (coverage shard)), 0 failure, Lint, Type Check, Bundle Analysis, Governed Surface Queue Guard and every Changeset gate among the successes. Gate verdicts are read off those check-runs; nothing was built, run or re-run here, and the dev's local unions, probes, ablations and bundle delta are read as declared. One corroborating read outside the inputs, stated so it is not hidden: the sibling objectstack checkout's `packages/spec` source (version string 17.7.0) shows `ListViewOverlayOptionsSchema` as a strict object over `listViewKindBlocks()`, declared on the list overlay member only, with the `grid` guidance the PR quotes; the verdict does not rest on it, because the PR's own pin measures the installed spec and is green under the Test shards.

### ① Derived judgments

Zod accept sets (`@object-ui/types/zod`: the `ListViewSchema` mirror, the tolerant `AnyComponentSchema`, the strict `StrictAnyComponentSchema`, and `safeValidateSchema`):

1. `ListViewSchema.options`: `z.record(z.string(), z.any())` with a three-key `.check()` to `ListViewOptionsBag.optional()`, where the bag is `stripImportedDefaults(SpecViewMetadataMembers.listOverlay.shape.options.unwrap())` extended with this package's `KanbanConfig`, `CalendarConfig.partial()`, `GalleryConfig` and `TimelineConfig` — RIGHT, under Q1 → A, objectui#8327 and objectui#10380 ruling A. It NARROWS every door: a key that is no kind (and `options.grid`, with the spec's own guidance) is refused at `options` with `unrecognized_keys`; an undeclared key in a kind is refused at that kind; a wrong-typed value is refused at its path; the strict face, which derived an open bag from the record, now derives the closed one. Nothing widens: the old record accepted everything the new bag accepts. No member is hand-copied: `gantt`, `map`, `chart` and `tree` are the spec's own blocks, and the four replaced kinds are the round-11 blocks, which are themselves the spec slots by reference plus refusal arms. The pin `list-view-options-bag-6152.test.ts` holds this in order: the installed overlay bag as a precondition (strict, the key set derived by the spec's own rule — a value of the list view's `type` enum that names a block — each kind strict and fully optional, and the authoring list view declaring no bag); the mirror's key set and error map identical to the bag's, with `kanban`, `gallery` and `timeline` the top-level blocks by identity and `calendar` the top-level block made partial; and verdict equality with the spec's bag over 17 documents, accepted and refused rows both present. All green under the Test shards.
2. The one sanctioned difference, the mirror writing no `chartType` default into a bag that did not carry it — RIGHT: objectui#8317's boundary rule, pinned as such.
3. The three refusals already in place (`options.kanban.groupBy`, objectui#8365; `options.calendar.dateField` / `endField`, objectui#8355) keep their messages and move from `custom` to `invalid_type` — RIGHT and stated in the changeset. The outcome and the string are unchanged; only the code moves, because the arm is now a declared member in both nestings. The 8355, 9653 and plugin-list 8365 pins re-spell exactly that, and the 8355 surface-2 row now also asserts the message equals surface 1's.
4. Every named refusal gives one message under `options.KIND` and under the top-level `KIND`, through all four doors, with its canonical remedy (`groupField` → `groupByField`, `cardFields` → `columns`, `imageField` → `coverField`, `dateField` → `startDateField`, `endField` → `endDateField`, `defaultView` with no home) — RIGHT; section 4 of the pin drives each arm through each door with a lit control that the bag app-shell relays parses.
5. `options.chart`'s legacy axes refused at `options.chart` with the spec's `unrecognized_keys` — RIGHT, the consequence of the bag by reference (the spec's chart block is dataset-bound). Block (e) of `object-chart-legacy-axis-keys-retired-10608` rightly flips from pinning the acceptance to pinning the refusal, with a dataset-bound control, and `list-view-dataset-chart-filter-refusal-10327`'s object-bound control becomes a dataset-less bag; what it guards (the filter refusal reads `dataset`) is unchanged.

Published TypeScript face (`@object-ui/types`):

6. `ListViewSchema['options']` becomes the eight kinds with no index signature — RIGHT, and no `objectql.ts` edit was needed for it: `ListViewSchema` is `ListViewAuthored & ListViewRuntimeProps`, and `ListViewAuthored` maps `ListViewInferred`, which is `z.input` of the mirror, so the face follows the bag. Section 6 of the pin asserts the closed key set and seven `@ts-expect-error` rows, live because `tsconfig.test.json` is in the package's type-check (Type Check green).
7. `ListViewTimelineConfig` is `NonNullable` of `ListViewSchema['timeline']` — RIGHT under Q2 → B: one declaration, the spec slot by reference, strict, `.partial()`, `dateField` refused by name. Keeping the export NAME as the derived type, rather than minting a new one, is the dev's declared way of doing B; it is equivalent to the answer and pinned by `Equal` in the types pin and in plugin-timeline's `timeline-date-binding`.
8. `ListViewGalleryConfig` retired from `objectql.ts` and from the `index.ts` barrel — RIGHT under Q3 → A. At this head the name survives only in the changeset, in one doc comment and in the pin's `@ts-expect-error` import; no package imports it. The remedy, the spec's `GalleryConfig`, is already re-exported.
9. `NamedListView.options` (`Record` of `string` to `any`) untouched — RIGHT: outside the surface, held by objectui#7928 Q2 (i), and the dev's note says so.

`@object-ui/app-shell` (the producers, Q1 → A):

10. `kanbanViewOptions` writes `columns` where it wrote `cardFields` — RIGHT; the renderer reads `columns` for the cards when no `cardFields` is present, and the census measured the node and the `$select` identical. `ObjectView.kanbanGroupByRetired-8213`'s residual set goes to `[]` with a control that it is empty and a new arm that `cardFields` is never written; `kanbanLane-8193` and `kanbanSummarizeField-11629` follow the spelling.
11. `galleryViewOptions` stops writing `imageField` beside `coverField` — RIGHT, conditioned as the answer conditioned it on the gate rung in judgment 14. The legacy READ (`gallery?.imageField` as the `coverField` fallback) stays, and `galleryBinding-7547` now pins both: a declared `coverField` goes out alone, and a stored legacy `imageField` still answers `coverField` and rides the block spread as stored.
12. `timelineViewOptions` stops writing `descriptionField` — RIGHT; the spec's timeline block has no such member, the bag refuses it, and the census measured that nothing drew the nested value. The one read that goes with it (`viewDef?.timeline?.descriptionField`) fed only that write, so this is the ordered producer change and not a reader retirement; the readers the fence protects (the alias fold, the `defaultView` lift, the two spreads, the collectors, `ObjectTimeline`'s `dateField` rung) are untouched, and the relay's forwarding of the stored, door-judged bag is untouched.
13. The new `ObjectView.optionsBagParses-6152.test.ts` parses each exported producer's block at the bag's own door for its kind, with a control that the door still refuses the three retired writes by name — RIGHT, and it is what keeps the relay's output inside the contract from here on.

`@object-ui/plugin-list`:

14. `availableViews` gains the `options.gallery.coverField` rung — RIGHT, the one rung the seat allowed (the objectui#8193 kanban precedent). Without it the coverField-only bag the relay now writes rendered a gallery the switcher never offered; the new pin `ListView.galleryOptionsBagCanonical-6152` answers YES for the canonical bag and for the bag app-shell writes, keeps the legacy and top-level rungs as controls, and answers NO for no block, a bag with no cover binding and an empty block. No alias read was removed.
15. The grid branch's `...(schema.options as { grid?: Record ... } | undefined)?.grid` cast — RIGHT, and the one line beyond the seat's fence, declared by the dev and stated in the PR's Acceptance notes: the typed bag no longer declares `grid`, so the legacy READ no longer compiled; the cast types it as the stored input it is and changes nothing at runtime. It is a reader kept, not a reader touched.
16. `README.md`: both examples author the top-level per-kind blocks (`kanban { groupByField, columns, titleField }`, `calendar`, a dataset-bound `chart`), `grid: {}` is gone, and a paragraph says a stored view may carry the legacy bag, which the write door judges with the same block schemas, and to author the top-level blocks — RIGHT; the typed `Schema` block compiles under Doc Snippet Type Check, and README Export Check is green.

`@object-ui/plugin-timeline`:

17. `ObjectTimelineProps.schema.timeline` keeps its type reference, which is now the narrowed `ListViewTimelineConfig`; doc comments say what it is and that the `dateField` READ stays until the readers' round — RIGHT under Q2 → B. The two alias fixtures (`timeline-date-binding`, `ObjectTimeline.absentDateAxisRefusal-7459`) keep their runtime value and each gains a real `@ts-expect-error` on a typed block carrying `dateField`; plugin-timeline's test leg reads `@object-ui/types` through the rebuilt `dist`, so a stale `.d.ts` would be red there (Type Check green).

Test instruments and pins:

18. `imported-defaults-8317.test.ts`: `IMPORTED` gains the bag as a row, and the census gains one enumerated category, `SCHEMA_RECORDS`, which accepts a read of a non-Zod record of schemas only when the WHOLE member chain rooted at the binding is the single argument of `stripImportedDefaults` — RIGHT. `VIEW_METADATA_MEMBERS` has no Zod internals and cannot be the direct argument, so the pin's own rule had no spelling for it; the new spelling still puts everything that crosses through the boundary, and the new leg pins that every entry is a non-Zod record whose every value is a schema, matched by at least one read, every read wrapped via its member chain. A one-hop read of the record, or an unwrapped member read, stays an offender. This is a test-side exemption category, not a published face, and it is the narrowest one that admits the crossing.
19. The eight re-spelled fixtures (`calendar-date-alias-refusal-8355`, `kanban-stray-group-by-refusal-text-9653`, `list-view-dataset-chart-filter-refusal-10327`, `object-chart-legacy-axis-keys-retired-10608`, plugin-list `ListView.test.tsx` and `ListView.strayGroupByRefused-8365`, app-shell `galleryBinding-7547` and `kanbanGroupByRetired-8213`) — each RIGHT: every flip is the narrowing's own consequence, and no assertion was deleted into a vacuum (the 8355 scope control becomes an undeclared-key control; the 10608 control becomes a refusal with a dataset-bound control).

Docs and changesets:

20. `packages/types/src/zod/README.md` gains the section on the bag by reference — RIGHT; Build Docs and Internal Docs Link Check are green.
21. Round 11's pending `.changeset/6152-list-view-blocks-strict.md`, which said the legacy bag was unchanged, carries a dated append-only note (+5 / −0, frontmatter and every prior line intact) — RIGHT under 「改成追加说明 (Recommended)」; Changeset Overwrite Report and Changeset Claim Re-read are green.

File surface against the claim 6070030626 as amended in 6070475966: every one of the 26 files is on the amended surface, "the tests beside these", or a dev-declared, seat-conditioned addition (the one `ListView.tsx` cast, judgment 15). The fenced paths are untouched: `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` and `ObjectGrid.tsx` (PR objectui#12010), the `ObjectGridSchema.defaultFilters` docblock in `objectql.ts` (the hunks sit at the two config types only), and every renderer-side reader. No governed surface is in the list, and Governed Surface Queue Guard is green.

### ② Semver level

- What the diff publishes: a NARROWING of `@object-ui/types` on every zod door (the bag by reference) and on the TypeScript face (`ListViewSchema['options']`, `ListViewTimelineConfig`), one export removed (`ListViewGalleryConfig`), and an issue-code change on three existing refusals; a producer change in `@object-ui/app-shell` whose rendered output is measured unchanged; one capability-gate rung and a README rewrite in `@object-ui/plugin-list`; and a prop type in `@object-ui/plugin-timeline` that narrows through its dependency, with doc comments. No accept set and no public surface widens.
- `.changeset/6152-list-view-options-bag.md`: `@object-ui/types` minor, headed "Narrowed (breaking)", with the FROM → TO mapping for every refused spelling and the one-line fix for each (`columns`, `coverField`, `startDateField`, the `object-calendar` element's flat `defaultView`, `chart: { dataset, dimensions, values }`, remove `options.grid`), the `custom` to `invalid_type` move stated, `ListViewTimelineConfig` under "Changed" and `ListViewGalleryConfig` under "Retired" with its remedy, and `app-shell`, `plugin-list` and `plugin-timeline` patch with what each changes — MATCHES what the diff publishes. objectui prices its own breaking changes as `minor` with the break stated in the body (the repo rule, enforced by Changeset Bump Policy, which is green), and the fixed release group carries all four packages at one version, so the three `patch` rows are the right declaration for packages whose own source changes no API. Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Overwrite Report and Changeset Claim Re-read are all success.
